title: Universal algebraic complexity beyond generic corner cuts
objective: Prove a new structural theorem determining or substantially narrowing the worst-case asymptotic number of monomial initial ideals of finite polynomial algebras, starting with three variables and seeking a mechanism valid in every fixed dimension. Establish the strongest relevant primary baseline first. Success requires a complete uniform proof of sharp growth or a substantial asymptotic advance over that baseline for all colength-n ideals or all n-point configurations, a rigorous further algebraic, geometric or enumeration consequence, reproducible exact certificates and an honestly scoped manuscript. Examples, reformulations, already known corollaries and a plan alone do not complete this goal.
relationship_to_previous_goal: A new research objective. The completed corner-cut counting manuscript and its acceptance records remain separate and unchanged in mathematical content.
aspirational_endpoint: Determine the sharp asymptotic order of G_d(n) for every fixed dimension and explain quantitatively when algebraic dependencies increase the generic corner-cut count.

second_feasibility_results.record: docs/interleaving_research.md, Second feasibility pass: interacting relations and a conditional count

all_socle_relation_spaces.hypotheses: I=J_D+R with D a finite monomial order ideal and R any linear relation space supported on its maximal monomials, in any field.
all_socle_relation_spaces.proof: Parallel downward chains from the maximal antichain are disjoint, so each total socle-coordinate sum is at most N-m <= n. Translating away the fixed standard monomials places the variable moment polytope in [0,n]^d. Apply the established lattice-polytope vertex theorem.
all_socle_relation_spaces.decision: Even arbitrary overlap confined to the socle cannot beat the generic order. Relations with surviving nonconstant multiples are required.

conditional_count.hypothesis: For an integer kappa>=1, every monomial box of volume at least kappa*n has quotient residues spanning the length-n algebra.
conditional_count.lemma: The first M=d^d*kappa*n monomials of every generic positive geometric order span the quotient. Greedy independence recovers its standard basis.
conditional_count.further_consequence: For fixed d and kappa, the minimum cardinality of a universal monomial-order list for this whole class is Theta_d,kappa(n^(d-1)(log n)^(d-1)), with the lower bound supplied by one generic point ideal.
conditional_count.scope: A conditional theorem, not an unrestricted bound or a new runtime theorem.
conditional_count.non_generic_control: The published seven-point F_29 configuration with ten initial staircases satisfies the rectangular condition with kappa=1, despite the generic count eight.

unrestricted_obstructions: For n diagonal points, kappa grows as Theta_d(n^(d-1)) even though g(I)=d for n>=2.

Translated Cartesian axis staircases give radical point ideals with g(I)=1, no identically zero monomial evaluations, and minimum representing-word/rank-completion length Omega_d(n^d). A uniform linear representative-word bound is false even for point ideals.
second_feasibility_results.completion_decision: Keep the full goal active. These supporting results identify the remaining mechanism and do not satisfy the all-ideal or all-point-configuration acceptance criterion.

binomial_count.conclusion: g(I)=O_d(n^(d-1)(log(n+1))^((d-1)^2)); in three variables O(n^2 log^4(n+1)).
binomial_count.proof: Known binomial normal forms give a partition residue matroid on the known hyperbolic cross V_n. Its moment polytope is the Minkowski sum of the n class hulls. Apply the published O_d(M^(d-1)) vertex bound with M<=|V_n|=O_d(n log^(d-1)n).

anisotropic_moment_bound.lemma: For an n-element staircase in an integer box q, 2*mu_i <= n*(q_i-1). The old lattice-polytope vertex estimate applied to any subcollection of coherent moment vertices gives O_d((product_i(n*(q_i-1)/2+1))^((d-1)/(d+1))).

fixed_curve_upper_bound.hypotheses: Every colength-n ideal over any field containing the primitive pure-power relations supplied by A=(A_1,...,A_d), positive integer A_i. The ideal need not be radical or binomial.
fixed_curve_upper_bound.sector: If i uniquely minimizes w_i/A_i, standard exponents satisfy a_j < min(n,A_i/gcd(A_i,A_j)) for j!=i.
fixed_curve_upper_bound.fixed_A_consequence: g(I)=O_A(n^(d-1)) for all finite quotients of a fixed monomial-curve ring, in every characteristic.

sharp_restricted_infinite_family.lower: For n=(d+1)m+e, m>=16d, independently take r_i in [m,m+floor(m/(8d))], i=1,...,d-1; set r_0=n-sum r_i. Weights w_d=d and w_i=d*(r_0-r_i)+i select exactly the n monomials in the d rays x_i*x_d^k, 0<=k<r_i, x_0=1.

sharp_restricted_infinite_family.lower_bound_cost: At least (floor(m/(8d))+1)^(d-1) distinct staircases for every sufficiently large n, including every remainder.
sharp_restricted_infinite_family.scope: Sharp only within this fixed curve. Its growth is below the existing generic lower bound; it does not improve F_d or G_d.

layer_upper_bound.lemma: If all staircases in a subcollection satisfy a_j<D, their moment vertices lie in O(nD) integer layers. Each layer has O(n^(4/3)) vertices by the established two-dimensional lattice bound, giving O(n^(7/3)D).

sixth_feasibility_results.record: docs/interleaving_research.md, Sixth feasibility pass: bounded connectors also limit sparse plane deformations

bounded_connector_lemma.hypotheses: Deleting k elements from a matroid leaves p direct-sum blocks; the joint internal element-order arrangement of those blocks has R open regions.
bounded_connector_lemma.bound: At most R*(p+k)!/p! distinct minimum bases under generic linear costs.
bounded_connector_lemma.proof: Insert the connecting elements in fixed order. On each previous-basis branch, the maximum member of a fundamental circuit from each block is fixed by its internal order; at step j there are at most p+j possible removals.
bounded_connector_lemma.distinction: Uses complete internal orders, not only component minimum-basis fans. The previous failed gluing shortcut remains false.
bounded_connector_lemma.priority: An elementary consequence of the standard matroid greedy and circuit-update rule; no novelty established.

hook_first_order_family.compatibility: An S-linear phi:M->B satisfies z*f0=y^(r-1)*f1 and z^(s-1)*f1=y*f2. Equivalently f0 is in span(y,...,y^(r-1),z^(s-1)), f1 in (y,z)B, f2 in span(y^(r-1),z,...,z^(s-1)).
hook_first_order_family.length: Exactly n=2m, with free K[x]/(x^2) basis given by the hook diagram D; proved directly using the syzygies.

hook_first_order_family.count: The variable residue matroid consists of a coloop and two blocks joined by three columns y^r,y*z,z^s. There are at most 6(r+s) internal order hyperplanes. The bounded-connector lemma gives g(I_phi)<=60*(1+H*(H+1)/2)=O(n^2).
hook_first_order_family.scope: Uniform over all compatible tail coefficients and all characteristics. Both surviving multiplication actions may be nonzero. This is below the existing generic n^2(log n)^2 lower order, and gives no unrestricted improvement.

seventh_feasibility_results.record: docs/interleaving_research.md, Seventh feasibility pass: interface rank, rather than corner count

linear_matroid_interface_lemma.hypotheses: Partition a finite vector configuration into blocks E_i with V_i=span(E_i). Put W_i=V_i intersect sum_{j!=i}V_j, q=sum_i dim(W_i), and let R count joint internal element-order regions under linear costs.
linear_matroid_interface_lemma.count_bound: At most 2^q*R distinct minimum bases under generic weights.
linear_matroid_interface_lemma.proof: In a fixed internal-order region every global greedy basis lies in the union of local greedy bases. Within block i, the columns increasing rank in V_i/W_i are forced globally, and exactly dim(W_i) local basis columns remain optional.
linear_matroid_interface_lemma.important_hypothesis: Intersections use the sum of all other spaces, not merely pairwise intersections. Three distinct lines in a plane disprove the pairwise replacement.
linear_matroid_interface_lemma.constructive_consequence: In three variables, per region refine only comparisons between at most q optional columns. At most 1+binom(q,2)*(binom(q,2)+1)/2 cells are needed, giving a per-instance list of O((q+1)^4*R) positive rational weights that recovers every basis.
linear_matroid_interface_lemma.algorithmic_scope: Uses the specified vector representation, exact rank calculations and rational cell operations. No new general bit-complexity bound or coefficient-independent class-wide list is claimed.
linear_matroid_interface_lemma.priority: Elementary linear algebra and the established matroid greedy criterion; no novelty established.

sparse_growing_corner_first_order_family.tail_classification: Writing A_Y=span(y^i:k<=i<r), A_Z=span(z^j:k<=j<s), W=Soc(K[y,z]/M), all module maps phi:M->K[y,z]/M have independently chosen f0,f1 in A_Y+W; f_i in W for 2<=i<k; f_k,f_(k+1) in A_Z+W. The full parameter dimension is 2m.
sparse_growing_corner_first_order_family.classification_proof: Adjacent plane monomial syzygies first force separated endpoint annihilation. The interior recurrence in degrees below k gives f_i=y^(k-i)*z^(i-1)*H, eliminated by the endpoint condition. Higher nonsocle components lie only on the two arms.
sparse_growing_corner_first_order_family.ideal: I_phi=(x^2,g_i-x*f_i for all minimal generators g_i of M).
sparse_growing_corner_first_order_family.length: Exactly n=2m, free over K[x]/(x^2), by the prior direct flatness argument.
sparse_growing_corner_first_order_family.blocks: After removing fixed columns and loops, two arm blocks have residue spaces in x*A_Y and x*A_Z. The core contains the k+2 generator columns and x*Soc(B).
sparse_growing_corner_first_order_family.interfaces: The interface dimensions are at most 3,3,6: only top-arm identity columns and two endpoint tail projections from each arm enter the core. Total q<=12 independent of k,r,s and characteristic.
sparse_growing_corner_first_order_family.internal_arrangement: At most H=10*(r+s+k+1)=O(m) internal comparison hyperplanes; arm columns form three progressions each and the central columns form two short parallel progressions plus four endpoints.
sparse_growing_corner_first_order_family.count_bound: g(I_phi)<=2^12*(1+H*(H+1)/2)=O(n^2), uniformly over all compatible coefficients and fields.
sparse_growing_corner_first_order_family.further_consequence: For each specified quotient, O(n^2) positive rational weights recover all its initial ideals using the proved optional-column refinement.
sparse_growing_corner_first_order_family.sparse_unbounded_corner_subfamily: For r=s=k^3, length has order k^3, the unavoidable staircase bounding box has volume of order k^6, and the number of corners tends to infinity. The result therefore goes beyond the earlier dense-box obstruction.
sparse_growing_corner_first_order_family.scope: A restricted obstruction below the existing generic n^2(log n)^2 lower order. It is not the qualifying unrestricted advance or a publication novelty claim.

untruncated_two_polynomial_description.scope: Every field and any number of polynomial variables; two nonzero polynomials and bounded convex lattice-complete multiplier domains. No quotient reduction is permitted.
untruncated_two_polynomial_description.common_factors: Remove the common factor to obtain coprime F_prime,G_prime. Multiplication by the common factor is injective in the polynomial ring and preserves the represented matroid.
untruncated_two_polynomial_description.kernel_domain: K0={h in N^d: h+Newt(G_prime) is contained in P, h+Newt(F_prime) is contained in Q}.
untruncated_two_polynomial_description.kernel_proof: Every relation is uniquely (H*G_prime,-H*F_prime). The Newton-product identity makes its allowed supports equivalent to H lying in the monomial space on K0.
untruncated_two_polynomial_description.coherent_bases: At any generic cost weight, choose the largest tagged term c from the G_prime support in the first input copy and F_prime support in the second. Delete exactly c+(0,K0); every other input column is in the coherent basis.
untruncated_two_polynomial_description.basis_count: At most |supp(F_prime)|+|supp(G_prime)| coherent bases, independent of multiplier-domain size. If K0 is empty there is one all-column basis.
untruncated_two_polynomial_description.projected_basis_polytope: T-S0-|K0|*C, where T is the total input cost-vector sum, S0=sum_{h in K0}(0,h), and C is the tagged Newton polytope of (G_prime,-F_prime) including the two input offsets.
untruncated_two_polynomial_description.constructive_consequence: Rank and the entire coherent-basis family are obtained from the erosion lattice set and the small tagged Newton polytope without minor enumeration.
untruncated_two_polynomial_description.limits: Convex lattice-complete multiplier domains and untruncated products are required. Common-factor multiplication can cease to be injective and Newton products can change after quotient reduction.
untruncated_two_polynomial_description.priority: Derived from the classical principal two-generator syzygy, Newton-product identity and complementary greedy criterion. Novelty has not been established; this is not an unrestricted advance.

factorial_prefix_minor.formula: For a,b>=0,a+b<=L, det[(L-1)!/(a+i-j)!]_{0<=i,j<b}=((L-1)!)^b*product_{j=0}^{b-1}j!/product_{i=0}^{b-1}(a+i)!, with negative-factorial entries zero.

factorial_prefix_minor.field_scope: Nonzero over characteristic zero or characteristic p>L-1. Smaller-characteristic ranks are checked separately.

one_variable_boundary_amplification.ideal: I_L=(x^2,z^L-x*A_L(z)) in K[x,z]. The checker adds y to embed it in three variables.
one_variable_boundary_amplification.count: Exactly L+1 global initial ideals over characteristic zero or p>L-1.

tenth_feasibility_results.record: docs/interleaving_research.md, Tenth feasibility pass: collisions preserve a fan, and sparse prefixes have Hermite defects

positive_collisions.scope: Characteristic-zero positive real nodes, fixed positive exponent tuple with A_1=1, and any multiplicity profile of total length n.
positive_collisions.rank_formula: min(n,number of distinct A-degrees), for every finite monomial set.
positive_collisions.proof: Sparse positive-root bound counting multiplicity, or classical confluent generalized Vandermonde theory.
positive_collisions.consequence: All such divisors have the same monomial initial ideal for every global monomial order and the same labeled positive Groebner fan. The free family q_epsilon=product_j(t-1-j*epsilon) preserves this fan while n distinct points collide to one curvilinear point.
positive_collisions.decision: Do not expand collision profiles as a fan-amplification search.

monogenic_embeddings.scope: Every finite-dimensional commutative unital algebra over a field of characteristic zero, in each fixed positive ambient dimension.
monogenic_embeddings.criterion: An algebra admits an embedding with the labeled generic corner-cut fan if and only if it is monogenic. Every monogenic algebra has a nonempty Zariski open set of coordinate tuples with that fan.
monogenic_embeddings.construction: For B=K[t]/(q), use x_i=(t+c)^(n^(i-1)) modulo q, outside finitely many excluded shifts c.
monogenic_embeddings.uniform_proof: For n distinct degrees lambda_j, the determinant of the remainders has degree sum(lambda_j)-n(n-1)/2 in c and nonzero leading coefficient product_{i<j}(lambda_j-lambda_i)/product_{r=0}^{n-1}r!. Mixed-radix degrees inject on the hyperbolic cross. The axis staircase proves the converse.
monogenic_embeddings.curvilinear_consequence: The fixed abstract algebra K[u]/(u^n) has both one-initial-ideal and C_d(n)-initial-ideal embeddings, the latter explicitly x_i=(1+u)^(n^(i-1))-1.
monogenic_embeddings.limits: Generic embeddings need not maximize the count. Intrinsic embedding dimension one and maximal multiplicity do not force a count smaller than generic. No small-characteristic extension is claimed.
monogenic_embeddings.priority: An elementary consequence of classical Vandermonde and open-minor arguments. The exact fixed-algebra formulation has not been established as novel.

sparse_geometric_prefix_defect.uniform_rank_defect: P_k=(y-z)^(2k-1)*(y+z) has sparse-staircase support, origin order 2k and order 2k-1 at (1,1). The functional ell_(i,j)=i!*j!*[y^i*z^j]P_k is a nonzero left null vector, so rank<=4k^2-1.
sparse_geometric_prefix_defect.exact_k2_control: Residual six-by-six matrix has a perfect support matching and exact rank five. Full sixteen-column prefix has rank fifteen. A saved five-by-five minor has determinant 2293235712.

Full tag powers on diagonal weights are treated by the separate support formula; the full positive fan remains uncounted.
sparse_geometric_prefix_defect.uniform_exact_rank: 4*k^2-k^2/4, for every even k>=2, by the graded Jordan rank formula and the established two-variable strong Lefschetz theorem.

graded_jordan_rank_formula.scope: Every graded Artinian algebra over characteristic zero, any homogeneous degree-one L, distinct scalar nodes tau_i and integer total-degree cuts a_i.
graded_jordan_rank_formula.proof: The established homogeneous Jordan decomposition splits each degree filtration into string prefixes. On each string their concatenation is an ordinary confluent Vandermonde matrix; Hermite uniqueness gives its exact rank.
graded_jordan_rank_formula.input_attribution: Iarrobino--Macias Marques--McDaniel Lemma 2.2 and Definition 2.28; classical confluent Vandermonde interpolation. Novelty of the combined consequence has not been established.
graded_jordan_rank_formula.sparse_family_consequence: Harima--Migliore--Nagel--Watanabe Proposition 4.4 makes y+z strong Lefschetz on the two-variable monomial quotient. Its Hilbert function gives strings start=i-1,length=R+k+1-ceil(i/2)-i. The exact prefix defect sums to k^2/4.
graded_jordan_rank_formula.full_algebra_consequence: For the actual algebra (M,x-exp(L)), positive diagonal weights (alpha,beta,...,beta) have minimum basis cost sum_strings(beta*start*length+c_length(alpha,beta)), where c_m sums the first m positive planar lattice scores. This treats all tag powers, not just two generator families.
graded_jordan_rank_formula.limits: Equal weights on the old variables are essential to the within-grade basis changes. This is not a full-fan count or a faster enumeration algorithm.

twelfth_feasibility_results.record: docs/interleaving_research.md, Twelfth feasibility pass: one-dimensional quotients of binomial algebras

uniform_theorem.scope: Every binomial ideal J of colength q>=2 and containing ideal I with dim_K(I/J)=1, in dimensions two and three, over every field. I has length n=q-1.
uniform_theorem.bounds: With M=|V_q^d|, g(I)=O(M*alpha(M)) in dimension two and O(M^2*alpha(M)) in dimension three. Thus the spatial bound is O(q^2*(1+log(q))^4*alpha(q*(1+log(q))^2)).
uniform_theorem.proof: The binomial parent gives q parallel classes. The child has a unique circuit on the support of its kernel vector, with other classes coloops. Choose each class minimum and omit the largest minimum on the circuit. The segment/triangle upper envelope, refined by every parent affine-patch boundary line, has the stated complexity by Pach--Sharir and its line-restriction overlay proof.
uniform_theorem.degeneracy_and_field_scope: Strict witnesses survive a small generic geometric perturbation; the algebraic reduction uses only the support of a one-dimensional relation and is characteristic-independent.
uniform_theorem.limits: This is a restricted consequence of established tools. It does not bound all ideals by the new exponent, certify novelty, or rule out a logarithmic improvement within the class.

finite_controls.scope: All 514 parent/child staircases have determinant/rank decisions; coherent cases have strict fully separated weights, independent Gaussian selection in all four characteristics and the omission formula. Independent incoherent cases have exact positive-dependence certificates. Includes a proper circuit, coloops, a nonreduced zero component and same-parent distinct-child witnesses.

twelfth_feasibility_results.known_prime_input: Chebotarev nonvanishing Fourier minors imply identical modular class-rank functions and fans for all equally sized subsets of a fixed prime orbit. Ordinary Vandermonde suffices for consecutive parameters for any orbit size; one-point deletion also works for every size.
twelfth_feasibility_results.decision: Do not enlarge one-point-deletion examples to infer n^(2+epsilon) growth: the uniform theorem forbids it. A periodic lower construction must analyze growing deletion defect or prove a logarithmic improvement. The next concrete lemma is a defect-sensitive bound for the sum of the r largest class-minimum costs; this remains unproved here. Keep the unrestricted upper route, strongest-current-primary audit and manuscript gate active.

thirteenth_feasibility_results.record: docs/interleaving_research.md, Thirteenth feasibility pass: deletion defect and the dual relation matroid

general_reduction.scope: Any colength-q binomial parent J contained in I with relation space I/J of dimension r, over every field.
general_reduction.formula: Minimum child basis cost = sum of all parent class-minimum costs minus the maximum weight of an r-column basis of the relation-row matrix H.
general_reduction.proof: The retained reference classes are a quotient basis iff coordinate projection of row(H) onto the omitted labels is an isomorphism. This is standard matroid duality, with a direct proof saved.
general_reduction.limit: The omitted classes are the r largest costs only when the dual matroid is uniform, or when another separate argument establishes that rule on the actual weights.

uniform_defect_bound.scope: Rank n=q-r uniform truncations of q nonempty parallel classes on M input points, in dimensions two and three; all 0<=r<q.
uniform_defect_bound.bounds: O(M*(r+1)*alpha(M)) in dimension two and O(M^2*(r+1)*alpha(M)) in dimension three, with constants independent of r.
uniform_defect_bound.proof: Within parent affine-patch cells, only triple intersections can be interior cutoff vertices. Independent sampling at p=1/(r+1) exposes them with probability at least p^3/4. Existing envelope bounds and binomial second moments give O(M^2*(r+1)*alpha(M)). Segment sampling bounds all parent-line crossings, and Euler counts the refined cells. Strict witnesses survive a generic point perturbation.
uniform_defect_bound.point_specialization: Any n-subset of a prime cyclic orbit over C, or consecutive parameters for any orbit size. The hyperbolic cross gives O(q^2*(r+1)*(1+log q)^4*alpha(q*(1+log q)^2)).
uniform_defect_bound.necessary_defect: For q=O(n), a lower family of order n^(2+epsilon) requires r+1=Omega(n^epsilon/((1+log n)^4*alpha(n*(1+log n)^2))). Polylogarithmic deletion cannot supply that exponent.
uniform_defect_bound.priority: Derived from established envelope bounds and elementary sampling, not certified novel; not an unrestricted advance.

application_assessment.architecture_scope: Architecture changes are within the intended ML research scope: build the model around usable algebraic structure and seek a proved advantage, rather than assessing only retrofit compression. fourteenth_feasibility_results.record: docs/interleaving_research.md, Fourteenth feasibility pass: the exact boundary of residual duality

uniform_colon_identity.scope: Every field, every containment J contained in I, on every global-order cone with in(J) a pure-power complete intersection. Neither radicality nor comaximality is needed.
uniform_colon_identity.statement: If C=in(J)=(x_i^s_i), q=product(s_i), n=length(S/I), and L=J:I, then length(S/L)=q-n, in(L)=C:in(I), and D(L)=c-(B minus D(I)), where B is the parent box and c its top corner.
uniform_colon_identity.proof: The coefficient of the top box monomial gives a perfect associative pairing on S/J. Orthogonal to I/J equals its annihilator, giving complementary lengths. The always-valid initial-colon inclusion and the equal monomial colengths give equality; reflection is involutive.
uniform_colon_identity.priority: Standard complete-intersection duality and elementary leading-term reasoning. Not certified novel and not a new unrestricted count.

grid_reduction.statement: For every univariate grid parent and every contained quotient, the child and its residual have identical positive initial-ideal fans, even when they are nonreduced and not comaximal.
grid_reduction.obstruction: Generic n-point inputs have n distinct values in each coordinate. Every grid parent has length at least n^d; the minimal residual has length n^d-n. This is not a general smaller-instance upper-bound reduction.

nonbox_countercontrol.information_loss: The nonbox parent initial has two socle monomials. Coloning the residual initial adds both, losing which individual corner was omitted.

fourteenth_feasibility_results.decision: Use residual duality only on proved box-initial cones. Retain the lost nonbox socle information and the compatible relation matroid in the general upper argument. The uniform lower route requires growing defect; a nonuniform fixed-defect route instead needs a multiplication-compatible mechanism outside the bounded socle-support class. Main theorem, further consequence, complete priority audit and new manuscript remain unachieved.

nonuniform_two_level_control.parent_definition: Union of the divisor boxes of x^3,y^3,x*z,z^4,y*z^3,x^2*y; monomial complement ideal J has length 17.
nonuniform_two_level_control.finding: Two independent circuit maxima exchange at different costs. There is no single uniform cutoff, even for a genuine nonbinomial quotient with commuting cyclic matrices.
nonuniform_two_level_control.limit: This witness is supported on the full socle and is subject to the existing O(n^(3/2)) support bound. It is not an amplification family. Uniform fixed-defect obstructions must not be promoted to every nonuniform fixed-defect construction.

uniform_family.parameters: Every even V>=4 and positive multiple U of V with U>=V, over every field.
uniform_family.child: I=J+(h_0), where h_0=sum_{a=0}^{U-1} sum_{0<=b<V,b even} y^a*z^b, of colength n=UV-2.
uniform_family.compatible_relation_ideal: R=span(h_0,z*h_0) has dimension two. On R, y is identity and x,z swap the basis; all variable actions are invertible. In characteristic zero this removes the points (1,1,1),(-1,1,-1) from the full torus graph.
uniform_family.matroid: A child basis omits the largest even-j and largest odd-j parent class minima. This is a nonuniform rank-two dual relation matroid, with all basis decisions characteristic independent.

global_upper_bound.proof: Y>X+Z eliminates y and gives a fixed x,z grid with two child states. X>Y has at most V(V+1)/2 parent regimes governed by two monotone cost thresholds, with at most six affine maximum candidates per color. all_ideal_bound.scope: Every finite-colength ideal over every field, including nonreduced ideals. Choose any monic coordinate elimination polynomials of degrees s_i and Q=product(s_i).
all_ideal_bound.proof: Every initial staircase lies in the elimination box. The known moment-vertex correspondence, addition of an integral unit cube and the established full-dimensional lattice-polytope estimate give the product-width bound.
all_ideal_bound.minimal_degree_consequence: For minimal elimination degrees s_i<=n, Q=n implies g(I)=1; otherwise r=min(n,Q-n) gives g(I)<=C_d*(r^d*Q)^((d-1)/(d+1)).

additive_rank_lemma.scope: Every field and every finite quotient whose coordinate elimination degrees all equal n, including nonreduced quotients.
additive_rank_lemma.statement: Every anchored monomial box has rank at least min(n,1+sum_i(a_i-1)).
additive_rank_lemma.proof: A proper subspace containing 1 cannot be invariant under a coordinate which alone generates the algebra; each multiplication step increases dimension.

minimum_bilinear_classification.hypotheses: n>=3, each coordinate alone generates the length-n algebra, and span(1,x_1,x_i,x_1*x_i) has dimension three for every i>=2.
minimum_bilinear_classification.conclusion: A=K[t]/(f), deg(f)=n, and all coordinates are nonconstant fractional-linear functions of t with unit denominators. No radicality, splitting or characteristic-zero assumption.
minimum_bilinear_classification.proof: A degenerate bilinear relation would be a zero product of two affine factors whose multiplication ranks are at least n-1, impossible for n>=3. Coprimality and Bezout make the denominator a unit.
minimum_bilinear_classification.exact_count: If pole-group sizes are m_j, g(I)=[z^(n-1)] product_j(1+m_j*z/(1-z)). All standard bases are unions of pure chains using at most one coordinate per group; every allocation has an explicit positive rational cutoff witness.
minimum_bilinear_classification.growth_limit: At most O_d(n^(d-1)), below the established generic logarithmic order. No stronger unrestricted lower family or certified novelty.
minimum_bilinear_classification.alternate_hypothesis: One anchored box with every side at least two has minimum additive rank 1+sum_i(a_i-1) strictly below n. This alone forces all the minimum bilinear ranks.
minimum_bilinear_classification.inverse_proof: Minimal growth forces a two-by-b rectangle to have b+1 rank. Its b-1 relations P(y)+x*Q(y)=0 have pairwise eliminants of degree at most 2*b-2<n, hence are polynomially proportional. Truncated relation dimension forces primitive degree one and includes multiplier 1; degree zero is excluded by multiplication-rank bounds. The argument extends to all coordinate pairs inside one unsaturated box.
minimum_bilinear_classification.integer_rank_gap: A cyclic presentation outside the fractional-linear class has rank at least min(n,2+sum_i(a_i-1)) for every box with all sides at least two. This extra unit is not a fan-count exponent improvement.

nineteenth_feasibility_results.record: docs/interleaving_research.md, Nineteenth feasibility pass: rank excess, exceptional ideals and extension bounds

rank_excess_tradeoff.scope: Every field, A=K[t]/(f) of length n>=3, with a second cyclic coordinate x, b>=2 and 2*b-2<n. The two-by-b product has rank R<2*b.
rank_excess_tradeoff.statement: There is a unique primitive rational ratio P/Q among the short relations. With m=max(deg P,deg Q)>=1 and E=(P+x*Q)A of dimension delta, R=b+m+delta. The quotient A/E has length n-delta, Q is a unit there and x=-P/Q.
rank_excess_tradeoff.proof: Eliminants have degree below n, so short polynomial pairs are proportional. Their multipliers are exactly the multiples of f/gcd(f,P+x*Q). Kernel dimension gives the exact sum of rational degree and exceptional dimension. Bezout makes Q a unit only on the retained quotient.
rank_excess_tradeoff.larger_rectangle: If a>=b>=e+2 and rank(a-by-b)=a+b-1+e<n, its two-by-b subrectangle gives m+delta<=e+1.
rank_excess_tradeoff.scope_limit: A small excess does not force degree one; quadratic exact maps and degree-one maps with one exceptional dimension both realize excess one. Nonreduced exceptions are ideal dimensions, not point counts.

bounded_extension_count.scope: Every field, ideals I contained in J in the same d-variable polynomial ring, colengths n and n-e, and all initial ideals of J having at most q minimal monomial generators.
bounded_extension_count.proof: For the same order the larger algebra staircase contains the smaller one. Each added box removes one available corner and creates at most d new ones. Count ordered e-step additions and sum over smaller initial staircases.
bounded_extension_count.fractional_linear_case: If the smaller quotient is the classified fractional-linear algebra of length n-e>=3, q<=d*(d+1)/2 and g(J)<=binom(n-e+d-2,d-1). Thus g(I)<=that binomial times the same product with q=d*(d+1)/2.
bounded_extension_count.asymptotic_limit: Fixed e gives O_(d,e)(n^(d-1)). If e=o(log n/log log(n+2)), the bound is n^(d-1+o(1)), excluding a fixed power gain. This does not exclude logarithmic gains for growing e.
bounded_extension_count.scope_limit: Requires coordinate-compatible containment, not an arbitrary abstract algebra map. The degree-two-and-higher rational branch is not covered by the fractional-linear consequence.

high_coordinate_degree_test.statement: In any length-n algebra generated by its coordinates, if s_1+s_i>n+2 and span(1,x_1,x_i,x_1*x_i) has dimension at most three for every i>=2, all coordinates are cyclic and fractional-linear in x_1.
high_coordinate_degree_test.proof: Affine multiplication ranks are at least s_i-1. A factored bilinear zero product would have positive Sylvester rank; a nondegenerate relation has a unit denominator whose inverse lies in the finite coordinate subalgebra. All coordinates then lie in K[x_1]=A.
high_coordinate_degree_test.sharp_boundary: K[x,y]/(x*y,x^m,y^m,x^(m-1)-y^(m-1)), with z=y+1, has n=2*m-2, all s_i=m and bilinear ranks three, but no coordinate is cyclic. Equality s_1+s_i=n+2 is insufficient.

twenty_third_results.record: docs/interleaving_research.md, Twenty-third pass: a uniform bound from lattice facets and planar shadows
twenty_third_results.scope: All fields and all colength-n ideals, including nonradical ideals, for each fixed d>=3. No quotient realizability assumption, simplicity, characteristic-zero restriction or generic configuration hypothesis.
twenty_third_results.geometric_theorem: For a full-dimensional lattice polytope P in R^d with V vertices, surface area S and expected uniform planar shadow size s, V<=C_d*S^(a/(a+1))*s^(1/(a+1)), a=d(d-2)/(d-1).
proof_mechanism: Primitive integer facet normals pay for incidences through triangulated facet lattice area.
Discard vertices incident to normals longer than H, at most d!*S/H.
The normalized determinant of d short independent normals gives spherical cone area at least 1/((d-1)!*H^d).
Stereographic projection and classical Euclidean isoperimetry give normal-cone boundary at least c_d*H^(-d(d-2)/(d-1)).
Rotational invariance of a random two-plane intersection with each edge-normal hyperplane exactly converts total normal-cone boundary to expected shadow vertices.
Dey convex-chain complexity plus Eppstein token reduction bounds each shadow of a rank-n residue-matroid basis polytope by O(m*n^(1/3)).
